authority: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI)
title: FSSAI Basic Registration — food business operators
breadcrumb: FSS (Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses) Regulations, 2011 › Chapter 2 › Regulation 2.1
text: Every food business operator (FBO) with an annual turnover up to ₹12 lakh, or a petty manufacturer with production capacity below prescribed limits, must obtain a Basic Registration under Form A. Application is filed through the FoSCoS portal. Registration is granted for a period of 1 to 5 years and must be displayed at the place of business. Operating without registration attracts penalty under Section 63 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

authority: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI)
title: FSSAI State Licence — mid-scale food businesses
breadcrumb: FSS (Licensing and Registration of Food Businesses) Regulations, 2011 › Chapter 2 › Regulation 2.1
text: An FSSAI State Licence is required for food business operators with annual turnover between ₹12 lakh and ₹20 crore, including manufacturers processing more than 100 kg per day, restaurants and caterers, and retailers/wholesalers/distributors above the prescribed threshold. Application is filed through FoSCoS with Form B. The State Food Safety Commissioner is the issuing authority.

authority: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC)
title: GST registration — turnover threshold for suppliers of goods
breadcrumb: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 › Chapter VI › Section 22(1)
text: Every supplier is liable to be registered under GST if their aggregate turnover in a financial year exceeds ₹40 lakh in the case of supply of goods (applicable in most states). For special-category states listed in Article 279A(4)(g) the threshold is ₹20 lakh or ₹10 lakh, as notified. Aggregate turnover includes all taxable, exempt, exports, and inter-state supplies of persons with the same PAN, computed on all-India basis.

authority: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC)
title: GST registration — turnover threshold for suppliers of services
breadcrumb: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 › Chapter VI › Section 22(1)
text: For suppliers of services (including mixed suppliers), the threshold for compulsory GST registration is aggregate turnover exceeding ₹20 lakh in a financial year (₹10 lakh for special-category states). Once liable, registration must be obtained within 30 days from the date on which liability arises.

authority: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC)
title: GST — compulsory registration regardless of turnover
breadcrumb: Central Goods and Services Tax Act, 2017 › Chapter VI › Section 24
text: Notwithstanding the turnover thresholds in Section 22, the following persons are required to register under GST irrespective of turnover: persons making any inter-state taxable supply of goods; persons supplying through an e-commerce operator required to collect tax at source; casual taxable persons; non-resident taxable persons; persons required to pay tax under reverse charge; and every e-commerce operator itself. Selling on Amazon, Flipkart, or similar marketplaces therefore requires GST registration from day one.

authority: Employees' Provident Fund Organisation (EPFO)
title: EPF — applicability and employee threshold
breadcrumb: Employees' Provident Funds and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1952 › Section 1(3)(a)
text: The EPF & MP Act applies to every establishment in a scheduled industry employing 20 or more persons, and to any other establishment employing 20 or more notified by the Central Government. Once covered, coverage continues even if employment falls below 20. Employer contribution is 12% of basic wages + DA + retaining allowance, with a matching employee contribution. Registration is compulsory via the EPFO Unified Portal within one month of reaching the threshold.

authority: Employees' State Insurance Corporation (ESIC)
title: ESI — applicability and wage ceiling
breadcrumb: Employees' State Insurance Act, 1948 › Section 1(5)
text: The ESI Act extends to all factories and to establishments notified under Section 1(5) — currently including shops, hotels, restaurants, cinemas, road-motor-transport undertakings, newspaper establishments, private educational and medical institutions employing 10 or more persons (20 or more in some states). Wage ceiling for compulsory coverage of employees is ₹21,000 per month (₹25,000 for persons with disability). Employer contributes 3.25%, employee 0.75%. Registration is via the ESIC portal.

authority: Labour Department, Government of Tamil Nadu
title: TN Shops & Establishments — registration requirement
breadcrumb: Tamil Nadu Shops and Establishments Act, 1947 › Section 5
text: Every establishment in Tamil Nadu that is a shop, commercial establishment, restaurant, theatre or other place of public amusement or entertainment must apply for registration within 30 days of commencement. Application is made to the Inspector of the local labour circle with a statement containing name of employer, address, nature of business, number of employees, and category. Fees are graded by number of employees. Registration is renewed periodically.
locator: Section 5, Rule 4 of TN Shops & Est. Rules 1948

authority: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
title: Udyam Registration — MSME classification and process
breadcrumb: MSME Notification S.O. 2119(E), 26 June 2020
text: Udyam Registration is a free, self-declared online registration for micro, small and medium enterprises based on both investment in plant & machinery and annual turnover. Classification: Micro (investment ≤ ₹1 crore AND turnover ≤ ₹5 crore); Small (investment ≤ ₹10 crore AND turnover ≤ ₹50 crore); Medium (investment ≤ ₹50 crore AND turnover ≤ ₹250 crore). Registration is via udyamregistration.gov.in using Aadhaar. It is a prerequisite to access PMEGP, CGTMSE, and most state MSME subsidies.

authority: Local Municipal Corporation / Panchayat, Tamil Nadu
title: Trade licence from local municipal body
breadcrumb: Tamil Nadu District Municipalities Act, 1920 / Chennai City Municipal Corporation Act 1919 / Coimbatore City Municipal Corporation Act 1981 › Trade Licence
text: Every trade, business or commercial activity carried on within municipal limits requires a trade licence from the local corporation, municipality or panchayat. The application is filed with the Public Health Officer or Revenue Officer of the local body along with premises documents, entity proof, no-objection from neighbouring occupants where required, and PCB/Fire NOCs where applicable. Fees vary by trade category and premises area. Renewal is annual in most local bodies.
locator: Local body Act, Trade Licence sections

authority: Controller of Legal Metrology, Government of Tamil Nadu
title: Legal Metrology — packer/importer registration
breadcrumb: Legal Metrology Act, 2009 › Section 18; Packaged Commodities Rules, 2011 › Rule 27
text: Every manufacturer, packer or importer who pre-packs commodities for sale, distribution or delivery must register with the Director of Legal Metrology. The pre-packed commodity must display: name and address of manufacturer/packer, common or generic name, net quantity in standard units, month and year of manufacture, retail sale price inclusive of all taxes, and consumer care details. Sale of non-conforming packages attracts penalty under the Act.
locator: Section 18; PC Rules 2011, Rule 6 and Rule 27

authority: Local body under Tamil Nadu Professional Tax Act
title: Professional tax — TN local body levy
breadcrumb: Tamil Nadu Tax on Professions, Trades, Callings and Employments Act, 1992 › Sections 3 and 5
text: Every person engaged in a profession, trade, calling or employment within a local body area in Tamil Nadu is liable to pay professional tax, subject to slab based on half-yearly income. The employer must deduct the tax from employees' salary and remit it to the corporation/municipality/panchayat where the establishment is located. The maximum annual liability is ₹2,500 per person per year in aggregate across the country under Article 276 of the Constitution.

authority: Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC), Ministry of MSME
title: PMEGP — Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
breadcrumb: PMEGP Guidelines › Eligibility and Subsidy
text: PMEGP provides margin-money subsidy for setting up new micro-enterprises. Maximum project cost: ₹50 lakh for manufacturing, ₹20 lakh for service sector. Subsidy is 15% to 35% of project cost depending on rural/urban and general/special category. Beneficiary must be 18+, individual (not existing unit), and must complete EDP training. Applications are routed through KVIC / State KVIB / DIC. Udyam registration is a prerequisite.

authority: Micro Units Development & Refinance Agency (MUDRA)
title: MUDRA — Shishu, Kishore, Tarun loan slabs
breadcrumb: Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (PMMY) › Loan slabs
text: MUDRA offers collateral-free loans through scheduled banks, RRBs, small finance banks, MFIs and NBFCs under three slabs: Shishu (up to ₹50,000), Kishore (₹50,001 to ₹5 lakh), and Tarun (₹5,00,001 to ₹10 lakh). Eligibility: any non-farm income-generating activity — manufacturing, trading, services. No processing fee for Shishu. Loan is disbursed against a business plan; no separate collateral, but banks may require personal guarantee for higher slabs.

authority: Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises (CGTMSE)
title: CGTMSE — collateral-free guarantee cover
breadcrumb: CGTMSE Operating Guidelines › Guarantee Cover
text: CGTMSE provides guarantee cover on credit facilities up to ₹5 crore extended by eligible member lending institutions to micro and small enterprises. Cover is 75% to 85% of the amount in default depending on category. There is no collateral security or third-party guarantee required from the borrower. Annual guarantee fee is charged to the lender based on outstanding amount and applicant category. Applied through the borrower's lender, not directly by the applicant.

authority: Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board (TNPCB)
title: TNPCB — Consent to Establish and Operate
breadcrumb: Water Act 1974 & Air Act 1981 › Sections 25/26 (Water), 21 (Air); TNPCB categorisation
text: Any industry, operation, or process that discharges effluent to water bodies, emits air pollutants, or generates hazardous waste requires Consent to Establish (CTE) before setup and Consent to Operate (CTO) before commencing production. Units are categorised Red, Orange, Green or White based on pollution potential. White category units are exempt from consent; others must apply through the TNPCB e-Consent portal. Validity ranges from 5 to 15 years by category.
locator: Water Act ss.25/26, Air Act s.21; TNPCB Public Notice 2016

authority: Tamil Nadu Fire and Rescue Services
title: Fire NOC — public assembly and high fire-load premises
breadcrumb: Tamil Nadu Fire Service Act & Rules › NOC Requirement
text: A No-Objection Certificate from the Tamil Nadu Fire and Rescue Services Department is required for occupancies that include public assembly (restaurants, cinemas, halls), high-rise structures, hazardous storage, or industrial premises above prescribed thresholds. Application is filed online through the Fire NOC portal with building plans and safety-measure declarations. NOC is renewable and inspection-driven.

authority: Ministry of Corporate Affairs
title: Entity types for a new business
breadcrumb: Companies Act 2013; LLP Act 2008; Partnership Act 1932; Indian Trusts Act 1882
text: A first-time entrepreneur can choose from: Sole Proprietorship (no separate registration required, unlimited liability, taxed as individual); Partnership (Partnership deed + optional registration; unlimited joint liability); Limited Liability Partnership (registered under LLP Act, limited liability, MCA filings); Private Limited Company (registered under Companies Act, limited liability, board and shareholder structure, higher compliance). Choice affects tax, funding access, and compliance burden.
locator: Companies Act 2013; LLP Act 2008; Partnership Act 1932

authority: Local Planning Authority under Tamil Nadu Town and Country Planning Act
title: Home-based business — zoning and residential premises
breadcrumb: TN Town & Country Planning Act 1971 › Land-use classification
text: Operating a business from a residential premises is subject to the local body's zoning by-laws. Certain low-impact activities — home tuition, small tailoring, consultancy, freelance services — are commonly permitted without commercial conversion. Manufacturing, retail with walk-in customers, kitchen for commercial cooking, or activities generating traffic, noise, or effluent typically require a change-of-land-use approval or shifting to a commercially zoned premises. Trade licence and Shops & Establishments requirements do not exempt on grounds of home-based operation.
locator: TN Town & Country Planning Act 1971; local building rules

authority: Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC)
title: GST Composition Scheme — small dealers
breadcrumb: CGST Act 2017 › Section 10; Composition Rules 2017
text: Registered persons whose aggregate turnover in the preceding financial year did not exceed ₹1.5 crore (₹75 lakh for special-category states) may opt for the composition scheme under Section 10 and pay tax at a flat rate: 1% for traders, 1% for manufacturers, 5% for restaurant service, 6% for service providers under the special composition scheme. Composition dealers cannot collect tax from customers, cannot claim input tax credit, and cannot supply through e-commerce operators required to collect TCS.
